parts.name: Shell Nav
parts.subtitle: Organism 42 · Move a reader between the sections of a framed brief: tabs in the shell bar on wide screens, and a menu button with a dropdown under the bar on narrow ones.

parts.name: Action Menu
parts.subtitle: Molecule 43 · Put every way to get or discuss one document behind a single header button, each item named by format and purpose.

parts.name: Status Strip
parts.subtitle: Molecule 44 · Say in one line where the work stands: not started and what is next, or which day it is, how many hours are done and what waits on the reader.

parts.name: Fact Tile
parts.subtitle: Molecule 45 · Give one fact a label, a figure and a short caption, with the label outside the box so a row of tiles reads as one aligned band.

parts.name: Day List
parts.subtitle: Molecule 46 · Tell the reader what happens on each day of a short plan, one plain sentence per day, from Before to After.

parts.name: Now Note
parts.subtitle: Molecule 47 · Tell the reader, in one sentence at the top, what to do now, and let them dismiss it once read; a changed note comes back.

parts.name: Summary Disclosure
parts.subtitle: Molecule 48 · Keep the whole plan one line tall until the reader asks for it: a title and a one-line summary when closed, the fact tiles and a quiet note when open.

parts.name: Pinned Details Card
parts.subtitle: Organism 49 · Show the details of the row the reader picked without leaving the full-width grid: a card pinned bottom-right on wide screens, a block below the content on narrow ones.

parts.name: Term Definition
parts.subtitle: Molecule 50 · Let a reader who does not know a word see its plain meaning in place, on hover, focus or tap, with a link to the full glossary entry.

parts.name: Display Preferences
parts.subtitle: Molecule 51 · Give every reader the theme switch and the reading options (easy-read font, larger text, roomy spacing) side by side in the header, remembered on their device.

parts.name: Plan Matrix
parts.subtitle: Organism 52 · Lay out a role plan as duties against time marks, every cell a proposal the reader can edit, with how they would know it is working at each mark.

parts.name: Cold Read
parts.subtitle: Organism 53 · Give a reader with zero context the whole page in one glance: who, what, where, when and why as labelled slots, how as before, during and after with real timing, and one line on how to read the rest.

parts.name: Signal Ledger
parts.subtitle: Organism 54 · Lay out a bull and bear read as grouped rows, each naming the signal it rests on and its evidence, with observed rows kept apart from the author's judgment.

parts.name: Sound Bite
parts.subtitle: Molecule 55 · Put one real quote at a time in the hero, typed out fast, with who said it, so social proof reads in a glance without a wall of testimonials.

parts.name: Fold
parts.subtitle: Organism 56 · Hold one section closed by default, with a summary line that states its verdict and a grade chip, so the reader can skim every verdict and open only what they need.

parts.name: Ledger Row
parts.subtitle: Molecule 57 · List keyed facts as rows, each with its chips, one line of evidence and its source, and show by fidelity which rows are proven, which are a reading, and which disagree with another record.

parts.name: Toast
parts.subtitle: Molecule 58 · Keep the one standing guard of a page in view (a stop-loss, a limit) without putting it in the reading order twice, and let the reader dismiss it for the session.

parts.name: Claim Check
parts.subtitle: Molecule 59 · Set what someone said beside what the record shows, with a state chip, so a reader sees at once which claims hold, which drifted, which are unchecked and which slipped.

parts.name: Heat Take
parts.subtitle: Molecule 60 · List the author's opinions from mild to loco, with the heat shown as a five-pip meter and a word, so the reader can tell a safe take from a provocative one without a colour ladder.

parts.name: Option
parts.subtitle: Molecule 61 · Lay out the live options for a next move side by side, each with what to do, its cost in time, and what it does for head, heart and wallet, with the leading option marked.

parts.name: Attributed Notes
parts.subtitle: Organism 62 · Record what a counterpart said about themselves in panels, each line timestamped and marked as their words, with unverified figures rendered in grain.

parts.name: Operator Pass
parts.subtitle: Molecule 63 · Record each review pass on a piece of work as a row: the lens and its question, what it found, and the ruling (held, changed or broke).

parts.name: Kintsugi Seam
parts.subtitle: Molecule 64 · Show a break in the work visibly, with what broke, how it was found, the repair and the guard that stops it recurring, joined to the next seam by a gold line.

parts.name: Question Pair
parts.subtitle: Molecule 65 · Set what the reader said beside the question worth asking about it, one row a point, so every question visibly comes from their own words.

parts.name: Give Get Table
parts.subtitle: Molecule 66 · Show a time trade step by step: when, what the reader gives, what they get back, so the cost of their time sits beside its return.

parts.name: Trace Steps
parts.subtitle: Molecule 67 · Show a method as three to four linked steps, each a key and its mark, over the one stop line agreed before the work starts.

parts.name: Spec Rows
parts.subtitle: Molecule 68 · Name a few labelled choices and what each one covers, as hairline rows in running text or as side-by-side cards when the reader is meant to pick.

parts.name: Strata Explorer
parts.subtitle: Organism 69 · Walk shipped work since April 2026 as stacked planes: services on top, then milestones, reversed beliefs, the inventions they led to, the posts written up and the proverbs minted, every link cited.

parts.name: Week Plan
parts.subtitle: Organism 70 · Lay out a plan week by week: what will be true by the end of each week, how it cascades from executive to surgical, where the kairos forks sit and what must be true at each, and how best, base and worst play out, with keep and kill switches, on-ramps, off-ramps, opportunity cost and stop-losses on one color-coded sparkline.

parts.name: Proof Lockup
parts.subtitle: Organism 71 · Greet a cold reader with the two to four proofs behind a claim, each a figure they can check, between one short framing line and the promise it buys them.
